correctness.rationale: Orient all r paths from common a to b and encode every edge homomorphism into Cq by unique ±1 increments (q odd>=5). Each path sum si has parity Li, |si|<=Li and all si congruent mod q, so w_i=(si−s1)/q∈Z; conversely all Tw displacement solutions yield colorings. Recoloring an internal vertex swaps neighboring +/− increments and preserves all si; signed-word adjacent swaps connect all path arrangements of fixed sums. Recoloring an endpoint shifts all sums by the same 2 with unchanged winding. Tw is a single step-two arithmetic progression; when it has >=2 members, a feasible sequence of terminal moves and internal swaps moves root color by 2 mod q, hence visits every root color and connects the entire winding fiber. When Tw is singleton, endpoint moves are frozen and exactly q independent root-color components persist. Fujii–Iwamasa–Kimura–Nozaki–Suzuki Theorem 5.1 gives contractible iff orientation has a directed cycle, otherwise S1. A directed cycle in a theta graph uses one fully forward and one fully backward branch, exactly the condition max lower interval endpoint=min upper endpoint, i.e. |Tw|=1. Consequently c=# {w:tw>=2} circles and p=q*#{w:tw=1} point components; unfeasible w excluded and empty Hom handled. The general component-type theorem is correctly credited, while the winding-count part is independently derived.

value.rationale: The multi-branch theta network is a standard family with several independent cycles, and graph-homomorphism Hom complexes have rich disconnected topology. The explicit interval formula simultaneously counts all contractible and circular components across arbitrarily many branches and edge lengths, distinguishing frozen winding classes from flexible ones. This improves a mere component-type dichotomy into a practical, nontrivial infinite-family topology classification.
residual_risks: It does not classify even-cycle targets, q=3, or graphs with cross-branch edges.

limitations: Only ordinary Lovasz Hom complexes, odd target cycles at least five, and >=3 internally disjoint branches each >=2 edges.
General theorem of Fujii et al is explicitly needed for the component homotopy type; new proof is the arithmetic component count.
